statement.text:
(W. Kimmerle). The prime graph (or Gruenberg–Kegel graph) Γ(X) of a group
X has vertices labeled by primes appearing as orders of elements in X; two distinct
primes p and q are adjacent in Γ(X) if and only if X contains an element of order pq.
Denote by V(ZG) the group of normalized units of the integral group ring of a group
G. Is it true that for each finite group G the prime graphs of G and V(ZG) coincide?
    This question has been reduced to almost simple groups (W. Kimmerle, A. Kono-
valov, Internat. J. Algebra Comput., 27 (2017), 619–631).       A. Bächle, L. Margolis
